snippets.output: There are several anti-nausea medications, known as antiemetics, that can help patients keep fluids down and are particularly useful in managing nausea and vomiting.

Ondansetron is a serotonin 5-HT3 receptor antagonist commonly used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or surgery, and is available in oral, intravenous, and dissolvable tablet forms.

Metoclopramide is a dopamine antagonist that enhances gastrointestinal motility and is used to treat nausea and vomiting associated with gastroparesis, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and postoperative conditions.
Prochlorperazine is a dopamine (D2) receptor antagonist effective in treating severe nausea and vomiting, including that caused by migraines and chemotherapy.
Promethazine is an antihistamine with antiemetic properties, often used to treat motion sickness, nausea, and vomiting.
Dimenhydrinate is an antihistamine commonly used to prevent and treat nausea, vomiting, and dizziness caused by motion sickness.
Scopolamine is an anticholinergic agent often used as a transdermal patch to prevent motion sickness and postoperative nausea and vomiting.
